title: A large number of protestors had gathered at Jantar Mantar carrying banners, posters and saffron flags and raised slogans against caste-based reservation.
author: PTI
content_html:
Union Minister Ramdas Athawale has demanded that sedition charges be invoked against those opposing or seeking abolition of reservation, which he called a constitutional right.

In a statement issued on Sunday (August 23, 2026), Mr. Athawale said protests against quota, including those at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, had brought the issue back into focus. He claimed that campaigns were also running on social media, calling for the removal or changes to the quota system.

“Opposition to reservation is opposition to the Constitution. Those taking an anti-reservation stand are anti-constitutional and stringent action of sedition should be taken against them,” the Republican Party of India (Athawale) chief said.

Some people were demanding the abolition of reservation, he said, asserting that reservation cannot be abolished as it is a constitutional right.

The Delhi Police on Sunday (August 23) said no permission has been granted to any individual or organisation to hold a protest or gathering at Jantar Mantar over reservation reforms and warned people against assembling there based on “misleading” social media posts.

A large number of protestors had gathered at Jantar Mantar carrying banners, posters and saffron flags and raised slogans against caste-based reservation.

The protestors were demanding that economic criteria be given precedence over caste in determining eligibility for government support and reservation.

title: Rajasthan High Court questions police as probe into attack on Dalit family changes hands six times
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The police investigation into a case of alleged land encroachment and attack on a Dalit family in Rajasthan’s Bharatpur district changed hands six times in the last two years, prompting the High Court to intervene. There was also a complete absence of supervisory review of the pending probe.

The victim, Jitendra Kumar, 24, a resident of Bharatpur’s Bayana block, moved the High Court seeking a fair investigation, completion of the probe and filing of a chargesheet in the case. The first information report (FIR) was registered on May 10, 2024, following an attack on Mr. Kumar and his family members.

The “politically influential” people who allegedly attacked the Dalit family in Kair village in a bid to encroach upon its agricultural land also registered an FIR against the victims. Though the police found the counter-case to be frivolous, the original case has been probed by as many as six investigating officers without any conclusion.

“Despite the lapse of 26 months and a provision in the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, for completion of probe in 60 days, the police have failed to act,” Mr. Kumar said in his writ petition. The investigating officers included a Circle Officer and five Additional Superintendents of Police, including one serving in the civil rights cell.

The offences for which 12 accused belonging to the Gujjar community were booked under the Indian Penal Code and the SC/ST (PoA) Act included rioting, attempt to commit culpable homicide, causing grievous hurt, unlawful assembly, criminal trespass and criminal intimidation.

The present investigating officer, Dinesh Kumar Meena, stated in the High Court that the offences against the accused had been proved and the result of the probe would be submitted in the trial court within two weeks.

Justice Shubha Mehta at the High Court’s Jaipur Bench observed earlier this week that the failure to complete the investigation in time was “concerning” and no satisfactory reason had been given for the delay. The petitioner also stated that calling him to join the probe every time after the change of hands amounted to his harassment.

The court directed the Public Prosecutor to obtain affidavits from all investigating officers named in the factual report, “explaining why the probe was not completed in 60 days and reasons for the subsequent delay”. Similar affidavits were also sought from the officers forming the supervisory committee under Rule 7(3) of the SC/ST (PoA) Act.

Welcoming the High Court’s order, the Centre for Dalit Rights (CDR) said here on Sunday (August 23, 2026) that the investigation could have been completed and the accused arrested if the authorities had complied with the statutory review mechanism. The matter will come up in the court for further hearing on September 7.

The members of the supervisory committee include the Home Secretary, Director General of Police, Social Justice & Empowerment Secretary, and Director of Prosecution. CDR Director Satish Kumar said though the committee was required to review pending cases under the SC/ST (PoA) Act once every quarter, the meetings were not held regularly and no relief was granted to Dalit victims.

title: ED arrests two in pan-India cyber fraud crackdown case
author: PTI
content_html:
The Enforcement Directorate has arrested two persons as part of its money laundering investigation into an alleged pan-India cyber fraud and digital arrests case involving transactions worth ₹30,000 crore, sources said on Monday (August 24, 2026).

They told PTI that Fahim Moin Hussain Sayed and Naim Mueen Sayyed were taken into custody on Sunday (August 23, 2026) from Mumbai.

The ED probe, according to the sources, was initiated after a Goa woman was allegedly duped after she was made to transfer ₹2.60 crore between May and June 2025 into some so-called "Secret Supervision Accounts" by the cyber fraudsters following a digital arrest.

The agency under the Union Ministry of Finance's Department of Revenue subsequently produced them before a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Mumbai on Sunday (August 23, 2026), which handed over their transit remand to the ED for taking them to Panaji, Goa, where the case is registered, the sources said.

The agency is expected to produce them before a special court in Panaji on Monday (August 24, 2026) seeking their remand for custodial interrogation.

The agency, during the investigation, found the money cheated from the victim was taken into bank accounts, withdrawn in cash and then converted into foreign currency through RBI-licensed money changers.

The sources said the agency suspects bank transactions worth ₹27,000 crore and cash dealings of ₹3,000 crore by this alleged cyber criminal network, which reportedly figures in as many as 300 victim complaints and 150-160 FIRs filed across 20 States and Union Territories.

The reported fraud with the victims is estimated to be around ₹4,000 crore, the sources said.

The ED has conducted two rounds of searches in this case in Goa and Mumbai in July and the latest on August 21, seizing about ₹3.25 crore in cash, the sources said.

The money trail found that the shell or dummy companies involved had drivers and employees living in single-room accommodations as the directors, a classic modus operandi in such cases.

title: Police used excessive force during Delhi protests: Amnesty
author: AFP
content_html:
Police used excessive force, including electric shock devices and pellet guns, against youth-led protests that forced Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign last month, Amnesty International said Monday (August 24, 2026).

A report from the rights' group clashes with the police account that force was used only after protesters turned violent, and comes after the Supreme Court set up a panel on Thursday (August 20, 2026) to investigate violence by both police and demonstrators.

Demonstrations in New Delhi, triggered by the leak of NET-UG paper, turned violent on July 20 when thousands of protesters attempted to march towards Parliament.

Amnesty said witness testimony and visual evidence it had verified confirmed the use of "pellet-firing shotguns, tear gas launchers, grenades, batons and electric shock devices against protesters" in Delhi and Bihar.

Amnesty said it had also verified two instances of a police officer "unlawfully using lethal force against a crowd" in Bihar's Siwan district. No one was killed. "The weapons were deployed in a manner that breached international law and standards and domestic policing guidelines," it added.

Amnesty said that there were "isolated incidents of protesters throwing stones", but that the "heavy-handed response was state-sanctioned violence masked as crowd control."

Delhi Police said in a Supreme Court hearing last week they had used force only after protesters "resorted to violence". They said anti-social elements "masquerading as aggrieved students" caused "grievous injuries" to security forces.

On Friday (August 21, 2026), Congress leader Rahul Gandhi staged a sit-in outside a Delhi police station with a 19-year-old protester who said he was injured by pellets during the demonstration.

Mr. Gandhi demanded a police investigation into the shooting, and officers later registered a case over the complaint.

title: Kerala HC directs strict action against illegal vehicle modifications
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Kerala High Court has directed the Enforcement wing of the Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) and the Kerala Police to impose strict penalties on all vehicles used in public spaces with illegal modifications in violation of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.

The court noted that the Enforcement wing had not taken any action against vehicles used in public places with wheels projecting outside the vehicles’ bodies, citing a specific instance of a modified four-wheeler, which had featured in the media after conducting rescue operations in Adoor that was impacted by the floods following the torrential rains in the first week of August.  

The Transport Commissioner informed the court that the offending vehicle, with six additional lights, was fined ₹5,000, and an additional fine of ₹2,000 was imposed for a pollution-related violation. The court sought a complete report on the action taken on this four-wheeler and whether any permission was granted for the use of the vehicle in a public place.

The Division Bench of Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna directed that each instance of unauthorised modification to a vehicle, such as after-market multifunction lights, red-blue strobe lights, wheel spacers and wide tyres, which result in the vehicle projecting laterally beyond the body of the vehicle, after-market exhaust systems with ‘flame-kits’, would attract a fine of ₹5,000 per alteration.

The court found that the use of such vehicles in public places without complying with the provisions under the governing laws would endanger the safety of other road users. The Motor Vehicles Act and the subsequent rules detailed every aspect of the construction and maintenance of vehicles, and if an aspect was not mentioned, it should be assumed that it was specifically excluded, the court stated.

title: Pune tribal students continue hunger strike for 10th consecutive day
author: Yohaan Varghese
content_html:
Students of the Government Tribal Hostel in Hadapsar's Gopalpatti area continued their protests and hunger strike for the tenth day on Sunday (August 23, 2026) over long-pending concerns regarding hostel facilities, safety, allowances, and the implementation of government measures for tribal students.

Six students are currently participating in the hunger strike — Shweta Girnak, 26; Nikita Mechkar, 22; Sharad Thokal, 26; Vijay Bhandble, 25; Rahul Dhanwe, 26; and Rajaram Padvi, 20.

Mr. Bhandble and Mr. Dhanwe were admitted to Sassoon Hospital on Saturday after experiencing breathing difficulties and dehydration, but they have been discharged and rejoined the protest on Sunday, according to Akshay Ghode, a protestor with the students’ movement in Hadapsar.

According to the memorandum submitted by tribal students, they have demanded the withdrawal of the Maharashtra government's August 14, 2026, Government Resolution (GR) concerning tribal hostels and the issuance of a revised order based on the November 11, 2011, GR, with changes to reflect current conditions and inflation. They have also demanded that allowances and other financial provisions be linked to the Consumer Price Index so that they increase annually in line with inflation.

Among their key demands is increased protection for students staying in tribal hostels and ashram schools and seeking an insurance cover of ₹10 crore for every tribal student, replacing the existing provisions under the Rajiv Gandhi student insurance scheme. This follows the recent deaths of three tribal students in a snake poisoning incident in Gadchiroli. The students have sought a compensation ₹1 crore each for the families.

The protesting students have also asked that pest-control measures to be carried out at hostels every two months instead of the existing six-month interval, citing concerns over student health and hostel cleanliness. They have sought the permanent display of the revised government resolution on notice boards at every government hostel so students can remain aware of their entitlements and facilities.

Another demand is for a safe and well-equipped central hostel building for female students in Pune. The memorandum also seeks the immediate filling of vacant posts in hostels and ashram schools, including posts for peons, security guards, and sanitation workers, either permanently or on a contractual basis until regular recruitment is completed.

The students have further demanded changes to the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Swayam Yojana, seeking removal of the condition that students can apply for the scheme only if they fail to secure hostel admission. They want students to be allowed to choose the scheme voluntarily while applying for hostel admission.

The memorandum also calls for all government and aided ashram schools in Maharashtra to be modernised and equipped along the lines of Eklavya Model Residential Schools. It seeks a separate and comprehensive law governing government tribal hostels and ashram schools across the State. The broader memorandum contains 17 demands concerning tribal education, employment, hostel administration, caste-certificate verification, and implementation of reservations in PESA areas. The students have warned that if their demands are not addressed, they may launch a wider democratic agitation across Maharashtra.

The memorandum has been submitted on behalf of students of government hostels in Pune city, with copies marked to senior government and social welfare officials, including the Social Welfare Commissionerate in Pune.

The students have sought immediate intervention from the authorities, saying their demands concern the basic rights, education, safety, and welfare of tribal students.

title: Three newborns die in fire at government hospital in Amravati, Maharashtra
author: Yohaan Varghese
content_html:
Three newborn babies died after a fire broke out at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of Amravati’s District Women’s Hospital, a government hospital in Maharashtra, at around 3.30 a.m. on Monday (August 24, 2026), prompting an emergency evacuation of dozens of infants undergoing treatment, according to Gorakhnath Jadhav, Senior Police Inspector, Gadage Nagar Police Station.

A ventilator exploded and caught fire on the third floor, killing three newborns with severe burns and smoke inhalation, according to Mr. Jadhav. Six infants were rescued from the affected area, and the fire was put out within 10-15 minutes, he said.

At the time of the incident, 39 newborns were admitted to the SNCU of the Amravati District Women’s Hospital.

Some children have been shifted to the Divisional Referral Service Hospital for further treatment. Of them, treatment of four children is ongoing, and one is serious, Maharashtra Revenue Minister and Guardian Minister for Nagpur and Amravati Districts, Chandrashekhar Bawankule, said in a post on X.

अमरावतीमधील आजच्या दुर्घटनेमुळे मी खूप दुःखी झालो. माझे मन हेलावून गेले आहे.

दगावलेल्या नवजात बालकांना अतिशय व्यथित अंतःकरणाने श्रद्धांजली व्यक्त करतो. त्यांच्या पालकांना हे दुःख सहन करण्याची ताकद ईश्वर देवो, अशी प्रार्थना करतो.
या घटनेच्या संपूर्ण चौकशीचे आदेश मी दिले आहेत. जे…

— Chandrashekhar Bawankule (@cbawankule) August 24, 2026

Doctors, nurses and other hospital staff rushed to the ward after the fire broke out and began evacuating the babies. Medical equipment was disconnected, and the infants were moved out of the affected area as the rescue operation got underway.

Mr. Bawankule said on X that he was deeply saddened by the accident in Amravati. “My heart is shaken. With a deeply grieving heart, I pay my respects to the deceased newborn babies. I pray that God grants their parents the strength to bear this sorrow,” he said.

Mr. Bawankule ordered an inquiry into the incident and said that the treatment of the injured is underway. “I have ordered a complete inquiry into this incident. Treatment of those who are injured is underway. They are being provided with all kinds of medical assistance, and facilities are being arranged so that they can recover soon,” he said.

“I am in constant contact with the district administration and have given all necessary instructions. The administration is fully vigilant. I have discussed this matter with the officers,” Mr. Bawankule said.

“The government stands firmly with the relatives of the deceased children, and the government and administration are providing complete assistance,” he added.

The SNCU provides treatment to premature and newborn babies who have low birth weight and are in critical condition.

Three newborn babies died after a fire broke out at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of Amravati’s District Women’s Hospital, a government hospital in Maharashtra, at around 3.30 a.m. on Monday (August 24, 2026), prompting an emergency evacuation of dozens of infants undergoing treatment, according to Gorakhnath Jadhav, Senior Police Inspector, Gadage Nagar Police Station.
A ventilator exploded and caught fire on the third floor, killing three newborns with severe burns and smoke inhalation, according to Mr. Jadhav. Six infants were rescued from the affected area, and the fire was put out within 10-15 minutes, he said.
At the time of the incident, 39 newborns were admitted to the SNCU of the Amravati District Women’s Hospital.
Some children have been shifted to the Divisional Referral Service Hospital for further treatment. Of them, treatment of four children is ongoing, and one is serious, Maharashtra Revenue Minister and Guardian Minister for Nagpur and Amravati Districts, Chandrashekhar Bawankule, said in a post on X.
अमरावतीमधील आजच्या दुर्घटनेमुळे मी खूप दुःखी झालो. माझे मन हेलावून गेले आहे.
दगावलेल्या नवजात बालकांना अतिशय व्यथित अंतःकरणाने श्रद्धांजली व्यक्त करतो. त्यांच्या पालकांना हे दुःख सहन करण्याची ताकद ईश्वर देवो, अशी प्रार्थना करतो.
या घटनेच्या संपूर्ण चौकशीचे आदेश मी दिले आहेत. जे…

August 24, 2026
Doctors, nurses and other hospital staff rushed to the ward after the fire broke out and began evacuating the babies. Medical equipment was disconnected, and the infants were moved out of the affected area as the rescue operation got underway.
Mr. Bawankule said on X that he was deeply saddened by the accident in Amravati. “My heart is shaken. With a deeply grieving heart, I pay my respects to the deceased newborn babies. I pray that God grants their parents the strength to bear this sorrow,” he said.
Mr. Bawankule ordered an inquiry into the incident and said that the treatment of the injured is underway. “I have ordered a complete inquiry into this incident. Treatment of those who are injured is underway. They are being provided with all kinds of medical assistance, and facilities are being arranged so that they can recover soon,” he said.
“I am in constant contact with the district administration and have given all necessary instructions. The administration is fully vigilant. I have discussed this matter with the officers,” Mr. Bawankule said.
“The government stands firmly with the relatives of the deceased children, and the government and administration are providing complete assistance,” he added.
The SNCU provides treatment to premature and newborn babies who have low birth weight and are in critical condition.
